p00-recall-q.text: Recall: what are the mean and variance of $1$, $2$, $6$?
p00-recall-q.name: p00-recall-q

p00-recall-p0.text: In words: how far each value is from the mean, squared, then averaged.
p00-recall-p0.name: p00-recall-p0

p00-recall-cue0.text: Look: compute mean and variance yourself
p00-recall-cue0.name: p00-recall-cue0

p00-recall-cue1.text: Look: purple line: mean; arrows: distance from mean
p00-recall-cue1.name: p00-recall-cue1

p00-recall-nav.text: Pattern Recognition · Week 3 · KP12 · page 1 of 12 · evidence-first trial · manual play: think at each question stop before advancing
p00-recall-nav.name: p00-recall-nav

p01-hook-title.text: Retrain on a new batch of data: is the prediction the same?
p01-hook-title.name: p01-hook-title

p01-hook-q.text: Same method, retrained on a new batch: is the prediction the same? Which is more stable?
p01-hook-q.name: p01-hook-q

p01-hook-a.text: Degree $1$: very stable, but the whole line is off the truth. Degree $9$: close to the truth on average, but varies a lot each time.
p01-hook-a.name: p01-hook-a

p01-hook-nx.text: Next, fix one position $x = 0.75$ (black dashed) and collect the $200$ predictions.
p01-hook-nx.name: p01-hook-nx

p01-hook-cue0.text: Look: guess first: which is more stable
p01-hook-cue0.name: p01-hook-cue0

p01-hook-cue1.text: Look: left: range of retrained lines
p01-hook-cue1.name: p01-hook-cue1

p01-hook-cue2.text: Look: right: range of retrained degree-$9$ fits
p01-hook-cue2.name: p01-hook-cue2

p01-hook-nav.text: Pattern Recognition · Week 3 · KP12 · page 2 of 12 · evidence-first trial · manual play: think at each question stop before advancing
p01-hook-nav.name: p01-hook-nav

p02-center-title.text: Where is the center of the distribution? How far from the truth?
p02-center-title.name: p02-center-title

p02-center-pf.text: In words: the truth is the average target at this $x$, without noise.
p02-center-pf.name: p02-center-pf

p02-center-q.text: Where are the two centers? How far from the red line?
p02-center-q.name: p02-center-q

p02-center-pg.text: In words: $\mathcal D$ is one training batch, $g_{\mathcal D}$ the prediction trained on it; the average over $200$ batches is $\bar g$.
p02-center-pg.name: p02-center-pg

p02-center-pb.text: In words: how far the mean prediction is from the truth is how far the center is off.
p02-center-pb.name: p02-center-pb

p02-center-cue2.text: Look: first: how far the center is from the red line
p02-center-cue2.name: p02-center-cue2

p02-center-cue4.text: Look: notation for the mean prediction
p02-center-cue4.name: p02-center-cue4

p02-center-nav.text: Pattern Recognition · Week 3 · KP12 · page 3 of 12 · evidence-first trial · manual play: think at each question stop before advancing
p02-center-nav.name: p02-center-nav

p03-spread-tw.text: Blue bar: one standard deviation each side
p03-spread-tw.name: p03-spread-tw

p03-spread-q.text: Which of the two distributions is more spread out?
p03-spread-q.name: p03-spread-q

p03-spread-pv.text: In words: how far each prediction is from its own mean, squared and averaged. Wider means larger variance.
p03-spread-pv.name: p03-spread-pv

p03-spread-sm.text:
Degree $1$: far off ($0.642$) but stable ($0.015$).
Degree $9$: almost unbiased, but more spread ($0.053$).
p03-spread-sm.name: p03-spread-sm

p03-spread-cue1.text: Look: first: which is more spread
p03-spread-cue1.name: p03-spread-cue1

p03-spread-cue4.text: Look: purple card: two kinds of error
p03-spread-cue4.name: p03-spread-cue4

p03-spread-nav.text: Pattern Recognition · Week 3 · KP12 · page 4 of 12 · evidence-first trial · manual play: think at each question stop before advancing
p03-spread-nav.name: p03-spread-nav

p04-split-title.text: Split the total error in two: why does the middle term vanish?
p04-split-title.name: p04-split-title

p04-split-thv.text: Green: above mean; red: below mean
p04-split-thv.name: p04-split-thv

p04-split-q.text: Can the mean total error $E_{\mathcal D}[(g_{\mathcal D}-f)^2]$ split into an offset part and a spread part?
p04-split-q.name: p04-split-q

p04-split-pa.text: In words: go from the truth to this batch in two legs: first to the mean (orange), then from the mean to this batch (blue).
p04-split-pa.name: p04-split-pa

p04-split-pc.text: In words: the cross term is $2 \times$ blue $\times$ orange. Orange is the same for every batch; blue is positive or negative with mean $0$, so the term vanishes.
p04-split-pc.name: p04-split-pc

p04-split-pd.text: In words: on average, total error is spread plus offset (squared).
p04-split-pd.name: p04-split-pd

p04-split-cue0.text: Look: think first: can it split in two
p04-split-cue0.name: p04-split-cue0

p04-split-cue1.text: Look: orange leg plus blue leg
p04-split-cue1.name: p04-split-cue1

p04-split-cue3.text: Look: expand: a cross term appears
p04-split-cue3.name: p04-split-cue3

p04-split-cue4.text: Look: $8$ more batches: blue legs both signs
p04-split-cue4.name: p04-split-cue4

p04-split-cue5.text: Look: $200$ batches: green and red halves
p04-split-cue5.name: p04-split-cue5

p04-split-cue6.text: Look: purple card: two parts add
p04-split-cue6.name: p04-split-cue6

p04-split-cue7.text: Look: numbers: two parts for degree $1$
p04-split-cue7.name: p04-split-cue7

p04-split-nav.text: Pattern Recognition · Week 3 · KP12 · page 5 of 12 · evidence-first trial · manual play: think at each question stop before advancing
p04-split-nav.name: p04-split-nav

p05-noise-title.text: What we really predict is a new $y$: add noise
p05-noise-title.name: p05-noise-title

p05-noise-lg.text: Orange: squared bias; blue: variance; gray: noise
p05-noise-lg.name: p05-noise-lg

p05-noise-py.text: In words: we really predict a new $y$: the truth plus some random noise. The noise has mean $0$ and is unrelated to the training data.
p05-noise-py.name: p05-noise-py

p05-noise-ny.text: Numbers: noise standard deviation $0.3$, squared $0.09$ (gray block).
p05-noise-ny.name: p05-noise-ny

p05-noise-pr.text: In words: one more block for noise. The new $y$ is independent of training data and noise has mean $0$, so the new cross term is also $0$.
p05-noise-pr.name: p05-noise-pr

p05-noise-ir.text: The gray block does not go away with another model; only more useful input features can shrink it.
p05-noise-ir.name: p05-noise-ir

p05-noise-cue0.text: Look: orange plus blue: the two parts from the last page
p05-noise-cue0.name: p05-noise-cue0

p05-noise-cue1.text: Look: gray: noise of the new target
p05-noise-cue1.name: p05-noise-cue1

p05-noise-cue3.text: Look: purple card: three parts add
p05-noise-cue3.name: p05-noise-cue3

p05-noise-cue5.text: Look: red card: noise cannot be removed
p05-noise-cue5.name: p05-noise-cue5

p05-noise-nav.text: Pattern Recognition · Week 3 · KP12 · page 6 of 12 · evidence-first trial · manual play: think at each question stop before advancing
p05-noise-nav.name: p05-noise-nav

p06-constant-title.text: Is zero variance good? A model that always guesses $0.5$
p06-constant-title.name: p06-constant-title

p06-constant-lg.text: Orange: squared bias; blue: variance; gray: noise
p06-constant-lg.name: p06-constant-lg

p06-constant-q.text: A model always predicts $0.5$ and ignores the data, so its variance is $0$. Is it good?
p06-constant-q.name: p06-constant-q

p06-constant-pk.text: In words: all $200$ predictions are identical, so no spread; but always wrong.
p06-constant-pk.name: p06-constant-pk

p06-constant-tkc.text: Zero variance only means unaffected by data, not accurate.
p06-constant-tkc.name: p06-constant-tkc

p06-constant-cue0.text: Look: decide first: is zero variance good
p06-constant-cue0.name: p06-constant-cue0

p06-constant-cue1.text: Look: three parts of the constant model
p06-constant-cue1.name: p06-constant-cue1

p06-constant-nav.text: Pattern Recognition · Week 3 · KP12 · page 7 of 12 · evidence-first trial · manual play: think at each question stop before advancing
p06-constant-nav.name: p06-constant-nav

p07-degree-title.text: Is a higher degree better? Squared bias falls, variance rises
p07-degree-title.name: p07-degree-title

p07-degree-q.text: As degree rises, how do squared bias and variance change? Which degree has the smallest total risk?
p07-degree-q.name: p07-degree-q

p07-degree-pm.text: In words: before we used only $x = 0.75$; here we compute all $101$ positions from $0$ to $1$ and average.
p07-degree-pm.name: p07-degree-pm

p07-degree-nm.text: Numbers: total risk for degrees $1$, $3$, $9$ is $0.326$, $0.124$, $0.157$; degree $3$ is smallest.
p07-degree-nm.name: p07-degree-nm

p07-degree-cv.text: This holds only for this design ($11$ training points, noise $0.09$), not "always use cubic".
p07-degree-cv.name: p07-degree-cv

p07-degree-cue0.text: Look: guess the trend of the two curves
p07-degree-cue0.name: p07-degree-cue0

p07-degree-cue5.text: Look: purple card: only for this design
p07-degree-cue5.name: p07-degree-cue5

p07-degree-nav.text: Pattern Recognition · Week 3 · KP12 · page 8 of 12 · evidence-first trial · manual play: think at each question stop before advancing
p07-degree-nav.name: p07-degree-nav

p08-weights-title.text: Going further: a prediction is a weighted sum of training targets
p08-weights-title.name: p08-weights-title

p08-weights-fh.text: $\hat y(x)=\sum_i h_i(x)\,y_i$; the values of $h$ at all positions form matrix $H$
p08-weights-fh.name: p08-weights-fh

p08-weights-ph.text: In words: a prediction is a weighted sum of the $11$ training targets; weights depend only on positions and degree, not on $y$.
p08-weights-ph.name: p08-weights-ph

p08-weights-nh.text: Numbers: each row of weights sums to $1$.
p08-weights-nh.name: p08-weights-nh

p08-weights-ps.text: In words: the noise of each $y$ is scaled by its weight and summed; the bigger the weight swings, the larger the variance.
p08-weights-ps.name: p08-weights-ps

p08-weights-px.text: In words: $H$ comes only from training positions; $\lambda$ is tiny and just stabilizes the computation.
p08-weights-px.name: p08-weights-px

p08-weights-cue0.text: Look: going further: two rows of weights
p08-weights-cue0.name: p08-weights-cue0

p08-weights-nav.text: Pattern Recognition · Week 3 · KP12 · page 9 of 12 · evidence-first trial · manual play: think at each question stop before advancing
p08-weights-nav.name: p08-weights-nav

p09-myths-q1.text: Myth 1: "as degree rises, total risk always falls then rises in a smooth $U$ shape." True?
p09-myths-q1.name: p09-myths-q1

p09-myths-a1.text: Not necessarily: degree $2$ ($0.332$) is higher than degree $1$ ($0.326$). The decomposition only guarantees the three parts add, not the shape.
p09-myths-a1.name: p09-myths-a1

p09-myths-q2.text: Myth 2: "if the model is a line, its variance is $0$."
p09-myths-q2.name: p09-myths-q2

p09-myths-a2.text: Wrong: a re-estimated line also changes with data (page 3: degree-$1$ variance $0.015$); only a line with fixed coefficients has $0$.
p09-myths-a2.name: p09-myths-a2

p09-myths-cue3.text: Look: myth 2: a line has zero variance?
p09-myths-cue3.name: p09-myths-cue3

p09-myths-nav.text: Pattern Recognition · Week 3 · KP12 · page 10 of 12 · evidence-first trial · manual play: think at each question stop before advancing
p09-myths-nav.name: p09-myths-nav

p10-practice-title.text: Your turn: which of two models is better?
p10-practice-title.name: p10-practice-title

p10-practice-lg.text: Orange: squared bias; blue: variance; gray: noise
p10-practice-lg.name: p10-practice-lg

p10-practice-q.text: Your turn: model $\mathrm{A}$ has bias $-0.4$, variance $0.25$; model $\mathrm{B}$ has squared bias $0.04$, variance $0.60$; noise $0.05$ for both. Which has smaller total risk?
p10-practice-q.name: p10-practice-q

p10-practice-hint.text: Hint: square the bias first; noise is the same for both.
p10-practice-hint.name: p10-practice-hint

p10-practice-why.text: Model $\mathrm{B}$ has much less bias, but its extra variance outweighs the savings.
p10-practice-why.name: p10-practice-why

p10-practice-nav.text: Pattern Recognition · Week 3 · KP12 · page 11 of 12 · evidence-first trial · manual play: think at each question stop before advancing
p10-practice-nav.name: p10-practice-nav

p11-exit-pl3.text: Total error: bias² plus variance plus noise
p11-exit-pl3.name: p11-exit-pl3

p11-exit-pl4.text: Trade-off: look at the sum of three
p11-exit-pl4.name: p11-exit-pl4

p11-exit-q.text:
(a) Bias $-0.3$, variance $0.02$, noise $0.05$: total risk?
(b) KP11: at $p = 0.8$, what is the fixed term $p(1 - p)$?
(c) What is the variance of a model that ignores data?
p11-exit-q.name: p11-exit-q

p11-exit-nx.text: Next (KP13): a structured probability model (logistic regression) keeps outputs between $0$ and $1$.
p11-exit-nx.name: p11-exit-nx

p11-exit-cue0.text: Look: three self-test questions, answer first
p11-exit-cue0.name: p11-exit-cue0

p11-exit-nav.text: Pattern Recognition · Week 3 · KP12 · page 12 of 12 · evidence-first trial · manual play: think at each question stop before advancing
p11-exit-nav.name: p11-exit-nav
